title: Krishna and his friend Sudama.
lines: This is a story from India, about friendship.
Long ago two boys went to school together.
Not to a school like yours, but to a school in the forest.
A wise teacher lived there.
The children lived with him.
They learned to read and to count.
They learned about the stars and about plants.
And they helped around the house.
They fetched water and gathered firewood.
One boy was called Krishna.
He was a prince.
He had blue skin and a peacock feather in his hair.
The other boy was called Sudama.
He was very poor.
His clothes were old and full of holes.
But Krishna and Sudama were the very best of friends.
They did everything together.
They laughed together.
They shared their food.
One day they went into the forest together to look for wood.
Then it started to rain very hard.
A storm came.
They sheltered under a big tree.
Sudama had a little puffed rice with him, in a cloth.
He gave half to Krishna.
They ate together under the tree while it rained.
Krishna thought it was the tastiest rice in the whole world.
When they grew up, they each went their own way.
Krishna became king of a big city, Dwarka.
He lived in a palace of gold, by the sea.
Sudama became a poor teacher.
He lived in a little hut with his wife and his children.
They didn't have much food.
Sometimes the children were hungry.
One day Sudama's wife said: Why don't you go to your old friend Krishna?
He's a king now.
Maybe he can help us.
Sudama felt ashamed.
I can't arrive at a king's palace empty-handed, he said.
I have nothing to give him.
His wife went to the neighbours.
She borrowed a handful of puffed rice.
She tied it up in an old cloth.
Give him this, she said.
Sudama set off.
He walked for days and days.
His feet hurt.
At last he came to the golden palace.
He stood at the gate, in his old clothes.
The guards looked at him.
What do you want here?
I'm a friend of King Krishna, said Sudama softly.
The guards laughed.
But they went to ask anyway.
When Krishna heard the name Sudama, he jumped up from his throne.
He ran to the gate, barefoot.
Sudama!
he shouted.
My friend!
He hugged Sudama very tightly.
He cried with joy.
He took Sudama inside.
He let him sit on his own throne.
He washed Sudama's tired feet himself.
Everyone in the palace stared with big eyes.
The king is washing a poor man's feet!
Sudama held the cloth with the rice behind his back.
He felt ashamed.
But Krishna saw it.
What have you got there, Sudama?
Have you brought something for me?
Krishna took the cloth and opened it.
Puffed rice!
Just like that time in the forest, under the tree!
He ate a handful.
Mmm, said Krishna.
This is tastier than all the food in my palace.
They talked all night.
About the old days, about school, about the storm.
Sudama completely forgot to ask for help.
He was just happy to see his friend.
The next day Sudama went back home.
Krishna hadn't given him anything.
No gold, no money.
But Sudama was happy anyway.
When he got to his village, he couldn't believe his eyes.
His little hut was gone.
In its place stood a beautiful house, with a garden full of fruit trees.
His wife and children were standing at the door, in new clothes.
They were smiling.
There was plenty of food.
Krishna had done it all, without saying a word.
Sudama looked up at the sky.
Thank you, my friend, he whispered.
Because a true friend helps you, even when you don't ask.
The end.
